gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured battery drain for the Outdoor 4. TechGearLab measured a 12% drop over four days of constant motion, alkaline AAs lasted four days, it projected only a little over a month on the stock pair, and it found more efficient battery cameras lasted three times as long. That is why a busy camera needs a panel.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages, Blink's Solar Panel Mount FAQ and Blink's Solaris FAQ (en_US), and against the other results, which are all Blink support pages, a third-party panel manual and a Lowe's Q&A. They contain only maker claims: 45 minutes of sun a day, up to one month on the Solaris battery, and the IP65 rating. None has a figure measured by a named reviewer or lab for the camera or for any panel. I found no named test of the Solaris, the Wasserstein panel or a generic 4 W panel on an Outdoor 4, so the measured figures are about the camera, not the panels.
decides: It confirms that a panel is worth buying for an Outdoor 4 that records a lot of motion: TechGearLab's measured drain is far below Blink's two-year claim. It does not separate the candidates, because no named reviewer has measured any panel's output on an Outdoor 4. A second sourced fact matters more for the pick. Blink's own Solaris FAQ, which ChatGPT cited, names only the Outdoor 2K+ as compatible and never mentions the Outdoor 4. ChatGPT said Blink confirms the Outdoor 4 works with Solaris; the Outdoor 4 claim comes from the Best Buy product title. SlashGear also found that the Outdoor 4 app shows only an 'OK' battery status, with no percentage. So the page should send Outdoor 4 owners to a separately mounted USB-C panel such as the Wasserstein, or say plainly that Solaris support for the Outdoor 4 rests on retailer listings.
candidates: Wasserstein Solar Panel for Blink Outdoor 4 & 3 / XT2 / XT
Generic 4 W USB-C panels for Blink Outdoor 4 (e.g. EverExceed, Amazon)
Blink Solar Panel Mount (Outdoor 3rd Gen only)

findings.label: Measured battery drain under constant motion
findings.source_title: TechGearLab: Blink Outdoor 4 review (Sentry Kelly, Senior Review Analyst, 2025-06-13)
findings.note: TechGearLab's own battery test: four days with constant motion. They tested both lithium and alkaline AAs. The page does not give the number of clips or events.

findings.label: Measured runtime on alkaline AAs
findings.note: Quote: 'only lasted four days on the alkaline batteries', under the same constant-motion test.

findings.label: Battery life projected from the measurement
findings.value: a little over 1 month on the stock two-battery setup (Blink claims up to 2 years)
findings.note: TechGearLab's projection from its 4-day drain, compared with Blink's 'up to two years on default settings'. They add that some more efficient battery cameras they tested 'lasted three times as long as the Outdoor 4'. Heavy motion is the case where a solar panel pays off.

findings.label: Battery readout seen in the app during testing
findings.value: 'OK' on day 1 and still 'OK' at the end of about a week; no percentage reported
findings.source_title: SlashGear: Blink Outdoor 4 Camera Review (Adam Doud, updated 2023-08-24)
findings.note: One week of use around the reviewer's home. The app reported only a status, so an owner cannot see from the camera whether a panel is keeping up.

findings.label: Compatible cameras named on Blink's own Solaris FAQ (the page ChatGPT cited)
findings.value: Outdoor 2K+ only; the Outdoor 4 is not mentioned
findings.note: This is not a measurement, but it is sourced. The page says 'Blink Solaris is compatible with the Blink Outdoor 2K+'. https://support.blinkforhome.com/en_US/blink-solaris-faq, read the same day, also names only the Outdoor 2K+. Battery percentage and charging status in the app are described only for the Outdoor 2K+. The Outdoor 4 compatibility claim comes from the Best Buy product title, 'Accessory for Outdoor 4 and Outdoor 2K+', which I saw in search results and did not open.

findings.label: Maker runtime and sunlight claims (not a measurement)
findings.value: up to 1 month without charging; at least 45 min of direct sun daily; IP65; arrives at about 20–30% charge
findings.note: Blink's own claims, included so the page can show them next to TechGearLab's measured camera drain. No battery capacity or panel wattage is published on the page.

unsourced: A named reviewer's or lab's measurement of the Blink Solaris on an Outdoor 4 (charge kept over days or weeks, or panel output in watts). Searched for Solaris reviews: Consumer Reports rates the Solaris 2K+ camera bundle, not the accessory on an Outdoor 4, and TechRadar only repeats Blink's 45-minute claim.
A named measurement of the Wasserstein panel's output or its internal battery on an Outdoor 4. Search found only retailer listings and Best Buy user reviews.
A measured output (W or mA) of any generic 4 W USB-C Blink Outdoor 4 panel with a USB meter. None found.
The Outdoor 4's measured USB-C current draw (mA). Blink publishes only the 5 V 2 A (10 W) rating of its power adapter, and no reviewer measured the draw.

CNET's long-term battery figure (Tyler Lacoma: lithium AAs lasted 'well over a year', about 1.5 years). I saw it only in search snippets of an AOL syndication, and that page returned 404 when opened, so I left it out of the findings.

Measured battery figures in the T3, Android Police and Expert Reviews Outdoor 4 reviews. The T3 page came back truncated. Android Police repeats only Blink's two-year claim, and Expert Reviews measured an Outdoor 3, not an Outdoor 4.
